Equilateral \(\triangle ABC\) with side length \(14\) is rotated about its center by angle \(\theta,\) where \(0 \lt \theta \lt 60^\circ,\) to form \(\triangle DEF.\) See the figure. The area of hexagon \(ADBECF\) is \(91\sqrt3.\) What is \(\tan\theta?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Four squares of side length \(4,\) \(7,\) \(9,\) and \(10\) units are arranged in increasing size order so that their left edges and bottom edges align. The squares alternate shaded and unshaded, as shown in the figure. What is the area of the visible shaded region in square units?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Sergei skated around an ice rink, gliding along different paths. The marked lines in the figures below show four of the paths labeled P, Q, R, and S. What is the sorted order of the four paths from shortest to longest?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A \(3 \times 7\) rectangle is covered without overlap by \(3\) shapes of tiles: \(2 \times 2,\) \(1 \times 4,\) and \(1 \times 1,\) shown below. What is the minimum possible number of \(1 \times 1\) tiles used?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

The coordinates of \(\bigtriangleup ABC\) are \(A(5, 7),\) \(B(11, 7),\) and \(C(3, y),\) with \(y > 7.\) The area of \(\bigtriangleup ABC\) is \(12.\) What is the value of \(y?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Buzz Bunny is hopping up and down a set of stairs, one step at a time. In how many ways can Buzz start on the ground, make a sequence of \(6\) hops, and end up back on the ground? (For example, one sequence of hops is up-up-down-down-up-down.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

The one-way routes connecting towns \(A,\) \(M,\) \(C,\) \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) are shown in the figure below (not drawn to scale). The distances in kilometers along each route are marked. Traveling along these routes, what is the shortest distance from \(A\) to \(Z\) in kilometers?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

A chess king is said to attack all the squares one step away from it, horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. For instance, a king on the center square of a \(3 \times 3\) grid attacks all \(8\) other squares, as shown below. Suppose a white king and a black king are placed on different squares of a \(3 \times 3\) grid so that they do not attack each other. In how many ways can this be done?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: Rotation preserves the common circumradius and makes the three triangles added outside ABC congruent. Subtracting areas determines their heights; coordinates then allow either a perpendicular-distance calculation or a radius-vector dot product to recover the rotation's tangent.
mappings.answerReason: ABC has area 49√3, so each added triangle has area 14√3 and height 2√3. Put the center at the origin and A=(-7,-7√3/3). The common radius is 14/√3, giving D=(-3,-13√3/3), with the negative horizontal coordinate fixed by 0<θ<60°. Thus cos θ=(154/3)/(196/3)=11/14 and sin θ=5√3/14, so tan θ=5√3/11.

mappings.rationale: A valid sequence has three up-hops and three down-hops, with no prefix going below ground. Grouping by the first return uses disjoint cases and products of smaller counts; alternatively, a recurrence can retain the hop count and current height.
mappings.answerReason: Writing U for up and D for down, the valid sequences are UUUDDD, UUDUDD, UUDDUD, UDUUDD, and UDUDUD. These are the five balanced six-hop sequences that never go below ground.

mappings.rationale: An elementary solution follows the one-way arrows, adds the marked distances along allowed routes, and compares the resulting whole-number totals. No unweighted graph-distance theorem is needed.
mappings.answerReason: The least distances from A to X, M, Y, and C are respectively 5, 7, 13, and 18. The last step into Z therefore gives min(7+25,13+17,18+10)=28. This is attained by A→X→M→Y→C→Z, with length 5+2+6+5+10=28 km.

mappings.rationale: Classify the white king's square as a corner, a noncorner edge square, or the center. Within each class, multiply the number of white-king positions by the available positions for the distinguishable black king, then add the disjoint cases.
mappings.answerReason: A white king in any of the 4 corners allows 5 black-king positions. Each of the 4 noncorner edge squares allows 3, while the center allows none. Thus the number of placements is 4·5+4·3+1·0=32.
